resources.string: Scan a barcode, take photos, or enter a label. Veguide shows what the evidence supports.
Camera looks up detected barcodes in public databases. A match identifies a product; it does not automatically make it vegan.
Photograph the front and the complete ingredients or materials. Tap Check to use your chosen AI when database evidence is missing.
Each evidence level has its own icon and color, also shown in History. Open a result to see its sources.
A verified certification applies to this exact product. A photographed label or a statement found online is shown separately.
A statement must refer to this product and variant. A vegan brand name alone is not enough.
A complete, resolved list can support a vegan composition. Processing aids, finishes and adhesives may need separate evidence. AI assessments are marked.
Missing information and animal-derived ingredients are different results.
Identified animal-derived ingredients or materials are explained in the result.
An incomplete label, an uncertain source or a failed request can leave the answer open. Add evidence with Edit, or retry the same item with Check again.
Documented animal exploitation can be flagged without changing the product verdict. Selling other animal products alone is not a flag. No flag is not an ethical certification.
No Veguide account is required. Choose how much to share and how many checks run at once.
History and photos stay on this device. Explicit AI checks send selected content to your provider. Database searches send product identifiers or search terms, never camera frames.
Close progress to check the next product. History and a notification show ongoing work. Offline mode stops network lookups. Replay this guide from Settings.
Run 1–10 checks at once. Provider limits still apply.
A certification source found online says this product is vegan. This is reported evidence, not independent registry verification.
A vegan claim or mark is visible on the packaging. Authenticity and the certification registry have not been checked.
Sources disagree, for example a vegan claim and an animal-derived ingredient. Both remain visible until the conflict is resolved.
